_about: Soundtrack 2050. b = projection block, d = seconds (Apple Music catalog; approx = estimate), p = plausibility, v = inspiration (editorial, out of 10). tg: mission | came (prediction came true) | tech (2050 technology) | film (from the film selection) | ru (Russian). imp = line for the import list.

tracks.t: Predicting the future for BBC Horizon
tracks.idea: Clarke says people will be able to work from anywhere on the planet, and that a surgeon in Edinburgh may one day operate on a patient in New Zealand.
tracks.proof: In 2001 a surgeon in New York operated remotely on a patient in Strasbourg. Remote work became normal after 2020.
tracks.q: Arthur C Clarke 1964 Horizon predicts the future

tracks.idea: An android in the family keeps the household's memories, and those memories turn out to matter most.
tracks.proof: AI companions are already a mass-market product; androids in families are not.

tracks.idea: People talk to an AI by voice, as they would to someone close.
tracks.proof: In May 2024 OpenAI showed voice GPT-4o, and Sam Altman captioned the launch with one word: “her”.

tracks.idea: A person and an AI sing one song together.
tracks.proof: The song was nominated for an Oscar. Neural networks have been writing songs with vocals from a text prompt for several years now.

tracks.idea: A rocket launch as part of an ordinary working day.
tracks.proof: Scientists around NASA JPL named Gattaca the most plausible science-fiction film. Rocket boosters now land and fly again.

tracks.idea: A person plays and an algorithm answers: two self-playing pianos pick up his notes.
tracks.proof: Arnalds made the album with Stratus, a system he built and also takes on tour. The machine is a co-author, not a replacement.

tracks.idea: Tokyo as an electronic city whose name is spoken by a vocoder.
tracks.proof: In 1979 this sounded like science fiction. Synthesizers and machine-processed voices have since become ordinary in pop.

tracks.idea: The song the android Yang remembers: a machine's memory can be tender too.
tracks.proof: The cover was recorded for the film. The original comes from Shunji Iwai's “All About Lily Chou-Chou” (2001).

tracks.idea: A robot teaches a gosling to fly and learns to care.
tracks.proof: The story is a fairy tale, but home helper robots are already in trials. The track is here for the lightness of the morning.

tracks.idea: “They’ll learn much more than I’ll ever know”: children will know more than we do.
tracks.proof: The safest forecast in this soundtrack: access to knowledge grows with every generation.

tracks.idea: Asimov says a computer in every home, connected to huge libraries, will let anyone learn whatever interests them at their own pace.
tracks.proof: The internet and AI tutors do exactly this.
tracks.q: Isaac Asimov 1988 Bill Moyers computers education

tracks.idea: A song first heard by a person in orbit.
tracks.proof: In May 2021 Coldplay showed the video to ESA astronaut Thomas Pesquet on the ISS before its public release.

tracks.idea: Moroder recalls deciding to make “a sound of the future” on a Moog modular synthesizer synced to a click track.
tracks.proof: These are the first two minutes of the Daft Punk track, so you can play it straight from streaming.

tracks.idea: All the music is played by a synthesizer; only the voice is human.
tracks.proof: Bowie recalled Eno calling it the sound of the future. Electronic dance music has since become mainstream.

tracks.idea: A lonely person looks for a partner through a computer: “I call this number for a data date”.
tracks.proof: Of heterosexual US couples who met in 2017, 39% met online (PNAS, 2019).

tracks.idea: A machine you cannot tell from a person.
tracks.proof: In 2025 GPT-4.5, given a persona, was judged to be the human in 73% of three-party Turing tests.

tracks.idea: Tenderness between machines: in Chris Cunningham’s 1999 video, robot Björk is assembled in a factory and kisses another robot.
tracks.proof: The robot arms in the video are ordinary factory equipment. Robots with feelings do not exist yet.

tracks.idea: People sing alongside Spawn, a neural network that Herndon and Mat Dryhurst spent years teaching to reproduce human voices.
tracks.proof: In 2021 they launched Holly+, a model of Herndon’s voice that others can sing through. Artist voice models are becoming an ordinary tool.

tracks.idea: Machine learning brought back John Lennon’s voice from a 1970s home demo.
tracks.proof: The voice was separated with a tool Peter Jackson commissioned for “Get Back”. In 2025 the song won the Grammy for Best Rock Performance.

tracks.t: Do chego doshyol progress (How Far Progress Has Come)
tracks.idea: “Robots do the hard work, and people are happy”: machines take over the work.
tracks.proof: Industrial robots and AI agents already do part of the physical and mental work. Whether that makes people happy is still open.
tracks.imp: Елена Камбурова — До чего дошёл прогресс
tracks.q: До чего дошёл прогресс Приключения Электроника

tracks.idea: A singer who does not exist: the voice is synthesized, and thousands of people write songs for her.
tracks.proof: Hatsune Miku has been sold as a singing synthesizer since 2007 and performs in concert as a projection.

tracks.idea: A concert of digital doubles: avatars on stage, the musicians at home.
tracks.proof: ABBA Voyage, with avatars by Industrial Light & Magic, has run in London since 27 May 2022.

tracks.t: “We choose to go to the Moon”
tracks.idea: Going to the Moon not because it is easy, but because it is hard. Speech at Rice University.
tracks.proof: Seven years later, in July 1969, Apollo 11 landed on the Moon.
tracks.q: JFK We choose to go to the Moon Rice University speech

tracks.idea: The music of weightlessness, for footage of the lunar missions.
tracks.proof: The album Apollo was recorded for Al Reinert’s documentary “For All Mankind”, made from NASA footage.

tracks.idea: Mission control polls each desk before the Moon landing, and each answers “Go!”.
tracks.proof: The track is built on real Apollo 11 communications from 1969.

tracks.idea: Docking by hand with a spinning station.
tracks.proof: The film’s science adviser was Nobel laureate Kip Thorne. The organ was recorded at the Temple Church in London.

tracks.idea: A waltz for the probe that chased a comet for ten years.
tracks.proof: ESA commissioned three pieces from Vangelis for the Philae lander touching down on comet 67P on 12 November 2014.

tracks.idea: The last man on the Moon sees a bright object through the window.
tracks.proof: The track samples Eugene Cernan’s voice from Apollo 17 (1972); NASA gave Daft Punk access to its mission recordings.

tracks.idea: A song about an astronaut, sung by an astronaut in orbit.
tracks.proof: Chris Hadfield recorded it on the ISS and released the video, filmed there, on 12 May 2013, before flying home.

tracks.t: Trava u doma (The Grass by the Home)
tracks.idea: The cosmonaut dreams not of space but of the grass by his home.
tracks.proof: It is called the anthem of Russian cosmonautics and plays at Baikonur on launch day.

tracks.idea: The question in the chorus: is there life on Mars?
tracks.proof: In September 2025 NASA reported a potential biosignature in the “Sapphire Canyon” sample collected by the Perseverance rover. It can only be confirmed on Earth.

tracks.idea: The rock and roll song that has travelled farthest.
tracks.proof: It is on the Voyager Golden Record (1977). Voyager 1 is now farther from Earth than any other human-made object.

tracks.idea: Sagan speaks of humans as eternal wanderers while the wall shows a jump from a cliff on Miranda and a flight over Titan.
tracks.proof: Every view in the film is built from NASA images and maps; the music is by Cristian Sandquist. It is the finale of the projection, so the film’s own sound plays here.

tracks.idea: A song from a series set in 2084: a plea to the future not to be cruel, and a promise to become better.
tracks.proof: It makes no technical forecast; it is about choice. That is why it closes the night: what 2050 looks like depends on us.

blocks.sync: Under After Yang, Her, Black Panther, Gattaca, Minority Report and 2040. Light and warm: AI beside people, cities, humans and algorithms together.
Under Ex Machina, The Creator, Blade Runner 2049, The Wild Robot and Hyper-Reality. Synthesizers, robots and AI that already sings.
Under The Martian, Interstellar, 2001, Oblivion and the closing Wanderers. Real missions, astronauts’ voices and Prekrasnoye daleko to end.

bench.note: A 65-minute generative piece: background while guests arrive.

bench.t: An der schönen blauen Donau (The Blue Danube)
bench.note: The docking waltz from 2001. About 10 minutes, to sync with the wall.
From the suite NASA adopted as music for the 2001 Mars Odyssey mission.
“Mars ain’t the kind of place to raise your kids.” Still true.
The last piece on the Voyager Golden Record.
Recorded with an early prototype of the MI.MU gloves, which turn gestures into sound.
Made by the Spawn neural network. Harsh; for a bold room.
The sound of the future from a film set in 2019. Video calls came true; flying cars did not.
“How rare and beautiful it truly is that we exist.” A quiet peak in place of Life on Mars?
Astronaut Ron McNair was to play this on saxophone in orbit. He died on Challenger.
Theme of the lunar mining base in the film Moon. 10 minutes long.
The Apollo 11 landing in First Man.
Soviet space disco from Riga, from the album Disco Alliance.
A short Interstellar theme for a quick transition.
